Modèle retenu : chaque carte est défectueuse avec la probabilité $p = 1/100$, indépendamment des autres, donc le nombre de cartes défectueuses dans un paquet suit la loi binomiale $B(10, 0.01)$ (valeurs exactes). questions.enonce_markdown: (a) there will be at least a defective card in a randomly chosen pack?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $X$ be the number of defective cards in a pack of $n = 10$. Each card is defective with probability $p = \frac{1}{100} = 0.01$, independently, so $X \sim B(10,\ 0.01)$ with

$$P(X = r) = \binom{10}{r}(0.01)^r (0.99)^{10 - r}.$$

"At least one defective" is the complement of "none defective":

$$P(X \ge 1) = 1 - P(X = 0) = 1 - (0.99)^{10} = 1 - 0.904382\ldots = 0.095618\ldots$$

**$P(X \ge 1) \approx 0.0956$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) exactly two defective cards are found in a pack?

The company offers a replacement guarantee if a pack contains at least two defective cards.

(c) What percentage of packs will the company have to replace?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A pack is replaced when $X \ge 2$. Use the complement:

$$P(X \ge 2) = 1 - P(X = 0) - P(X = 1).$$

$$P(X = 0) = (0.99)^{10} = 0.904382, \qquad P(X = 1) = \binom{10}{1}(0.01)(0.99)^9 = 10 \times 0.01 \times 0.913517 = 0.091352.$$

$$P(X \ge 2) = 1 - 0.904382 - 0.091352 = 0.004266\ldots$$

**The company will have to replace about $0.43\%$ of the packs** (about 4 packs in every 1000).
